hotspot_events.title: Panasonic Hukou CCL Plant Fire Impact Expands: Work Resumption Takes Months, Nov 1 New Round of CCL Price Increase Compounded by Glass-Fiber Cloth Price Increase
hotspot_events.heat_reason: ~4% of high-end CCL supply is impacted and work resumption takes more than several months, combined with the Nov 1 new round of price increases and glass-fiber cloth price increases, directly impacting high-multilayer/high-speed board lead times and costs
hotspot_events.summary: Follow-up on the Nov 4 fire at Panasonic's Hsinchu Hukou plant in Taiwan: this period confirms that work resumption will take more than several months; Panasonic is coordinating alternative supply from bases in Japan, China, and Thailand; Nov 1 new round of CCL price increases (M6 and below +15%, prepreg +25%, largest single round in two years); glass-fiber cloth price increases across the board on Nov 3 (7628 thick cloth +1.5 RMB/m, 2116 thin cloth +2.5 RMB/m); Shengyi states capacity is tight and expects further adjustments this month.
numbers: ~4% of global high-end CCL supply affected
Work resumption takes more than several months

hotspot_events.title: Extreme Spot Copper Tightness Unrelieved: Yangshan Premium Hits Record $230/ton for 3 Consecutive Days, Shanghai Copper Premium Hits All-Time High
hotspot_events.heat_reason: Futures pulled back but spot premium reached an all-time high, physical tightness remains unrelieved, directly driving up costs for copper tubes, copper parts, and cables
hotspot_events.summary: LME 3M closed at $13,896.5/ton (+0.93%) on Nov 9, pulling back to $13,679/ton (-1.56%) on Nov 10; Yangshan copper premium set a record $230/ton for 3 consecutive days, and Shanghai copper spot premium reached 2,615 RMB/ton on Nov 6, an all-time high; spot silver reported $52.36/oz (+2.21%) on Nov 11.
numbers: Shanghai copper premium reached all-time high 2,615 RMB/ton

hotspot_events.title: DRAM/HBM Shortage Worsens: SK Hynix Sold Out Through 2029, Q4 Contract Prices Forecast to Rise Another 13–18%
hotspot_events.heat_reason: Memory shortage expectations extended to 2029–2030, Q4 contract prices rise again, putting pressure on both memory costs and allocation for boards/cards
hotspot_events.summary: SK Hynix stated that DRAM and HBM are 'effectively sold out through 2029,' with shortages expected to last until at least 2030; October general DRAM contract price for DDR4 8Gb averaged $27.5 (+5.77%), and TrendForce forecasts Q4 PC DRAM contract prices to rise another 13–18%.

industry_updates.title: Johnson Controls × Armada launch Dublin modular AI data center production, first unit shipped to Norway
industry_updates.detail: Johnson Controls and Armada have started continuous production of Leviathan modular AI data centers at the Galleon Forge Two plant in Dublin. The first unit has been shipped to Fossefall in Norway, and the initial batch of 5 units totaling over 9MW will be delivered by Q1 2027, with both parties targeting a capacity of at least 500MW by 2027.

industry_updates.title: Daikin releases 60MW AI factory cooling reference architecture D60-W, with liquid cooling handling 92% of load
industry_updates.detail: Daikin released the 60MW AI factory cooling reference architecture D60-W: compatible with the NVIDIA DSX platform and Vera Rubin NVL72 racks, liquid cooling handles 92% of the load, centered around the oil-free magnetic-bearing Magnitude WME centrifugal chiller (maximum 10MW per unit), dry coolers replace cooling towers with zero makeup water; proprietary CDUs and data center dry coolers targeted for shipment in H2 2027.

industry_updates.title: Modine begins commercial production at new Grand Prairie chiller plant in Texas
industry_updates.detail: Modine's new 682,000-square-foot Airedale chiller plant in Grand Prairie, Texas, has commenced commercial production, specializing in 2MW and 3MW chillers with free cooling, targeting four 2MW production lines by the end of the fiscal year, making it its largest global Airedale chiller production base.

industry_updates.title: Lenovo releases "Wanquan Hybrid Token Factory" brand, signs agreement for first Zhangjiakou master factory
industry_updates.detail: Lenovo released the "Wanquan Hybrid Token Factory" brand and signed an agreement with the Zhangjiakou municipal government to establish the first master factory: initial planning includes a 15,000 P heterogeneous computing cluster, an intelligent computing center of about 100MW, annual token production exceeding 2 quadrillion, with an intelligent computing center PUE below 1.1 using full-stack liquid cooling.
industry_updates.source: Lenovo Group Official WeChat Account via Intelligent Manufacturing Network, 2026-11-10

industry_updates.title: Gree wins over 300 million RMB in China Mobile/China Tower thermal control centralized procurement bids, Dong Mingzhu discusses rising copper prices
industry_updates.detail: In the first week of November, Gree successively won centralized procurement bids for thermal control equipment from China Mobile and China Tower, with total order amounts exceeding 300 million RMB (products include air-cooled refrigerant pump computer room air conditioners and chilled water row-level air conditioners); on 11-10, Dong Mingzhu responded that the main reason for performance decline was rising copper prices (copper prices are about 5–6 times aluminum prices), and to ensure quality, the company insists on using copper, willing to sacrifice tens of billions of RMB in profits.

industry_updates.title: Vertiv stock rebounds for two days, recovering most losses from 11-05 plunge
industry_updates.detail: Vertiv's stock closed at $200.47 (+9.63%) on 11-09 and closed again at $206.51 (+6.33%) on 11-11, recovering most of the ground lost during the -14% plunge on 11-05 (Thursday); management stated at the Baird conference on 11-10 that AI and traditional cloud demand remain resilient, and provided an 800VDC roadmap (hybrid solution in H2 2027, native end-to-end system in H2 2028).
industry_updates.source: Finnhub/TipRanks Market Data, Reuters via ad-hoc-news, 2026-11-10

siphon_effects.detail: Combined 2026 capex guidance for the top four cloud providers is approximately $735 billion (Amazon approx. $220B, Alphabet $195–$205B, Microsoft approx. $175B, Meta $135–$145B), about 1.78x the $413.4 billion in 2025; Q3 single-quarter total for five companies (including Oracle) reached $237.3 billion, +95% YoY, with all four forecasting continued increases in 2027

SK Hynix stated that DRAM and HBM are "effectively sold out through 2029" with shortages expected to persist until at least 2030; October average contract price for DDR4 8Gb was $27.5 (+5.77%), TrendForce forecasts Q4 PC DRAM contract prices to rise another 13–18%

Samsung Electro-Mechanics lead time for AI server MLCCs is about 35 weeks (standard 12 weeks), raising prices for some customers starting Q4 (consumer-grade X5R +25–30%, AI server X6S +10–20%); Murata MLCC orders reached 1.47x sales, and expanding capacity by over 20% takes two years; TrendForce predicted on 10-29 that high-capacitance MLCC shortages will extend into H1 2027

Infineon announced on 11-09 the successful processing of functional devices on 300mm SiC wafers at its Villach plant in Austria (technology milestone); CRRC Times Electric stated on 11-11 that Phase I, Phase II, and Phase III Yixing chip production lines for IGBTs are all operating at full capacity, with the Phase III Zhuzhou SiC production line ramping up capacity in 2026 and expected to reach first-stage design capacity by mid-2027

A new round of price hikes on 11-01 (M6 and below +15%, prepreg +25%) compounded by the Panasonic fire led to a comprehensive price increase for glass-fiber cloth on 11-03, with 7628 thick cloth rising over 250% cumulatively from 4.15 RMB/meter at the end of Q3 2025; VersaLogic stated on 11-04 that multiple CCL plants have implemented allocation quotas, with high-performance material lead times at 24–32 weeks

Google announced on 11-05 a $1.7 billion investment to build its first data center in Laramie County, Wyoming, with a phase-one 702MW fuel cell power plant (built by AEP, supplied by Bloom Energy); Crusoe confirmed on 11-06 that it has sold the site to Google

cross_industry.detail: Transformer lead times have exceeded 5 years: HD Hyundai Electric stated that large power transformers from top-tier manufacturers have lead times exceeding 5 years (ordered in 2026, delivered in 2031); US imports of large power transformers above 60MVA increased from $900 million in 2022 to $3.1 billion in 2025; Morgan Stanley stated that US data centers will require 72GW of power from 2025–2028, with only 25GW secured or under construction

Solar-storage product price adjustment wave: Huawei Digital Energy plans to raise solar-storage product prices by 5–15% (notified on 10-20, effective date pending); Kehua Digital Energy raised all series by 5–15%, effective 11-01; Sungrow raised inverters/PCS/energy storage by 5–15% starting 9-20 — solar-storage and HVAC share capacity for power devices and electrical components, causing price hike signals to spill over

Mature node foundry price increases: Powerchip Semiconductor Manufacturing Corporation (PSMC) stated in an earnings call on 10-21 that it is negotiating another 10–20% price hike for logic foundry in 2027, with 80% of MOSFET and IGBT capacity locked in via long-term agreements; United Microelectronics Corporation (UMC) reported on 10-28 for Q3 a capacity utilization rate of 92% with multiple 12-inch fabs fully loaded, expecting average selling prices in 2027 to rise 10% compared to 2026 — cost and lead-time pressures are synchronized for MCUs, analog, and power ICs on mature nodes

Marvell announced on 11-02 the acquisition of optical communications giant Lumentum in an all-stock transaction with an implied enterprise value of $115 billion (4.5 Marvell shares per share, a 23.9% premium), expected to close in H1 2028, resulting in a combined 2030 TAM of $550 billion — this AI optical interconnect M&A confirms intensifying competition for optical transceiver and laser capacity

NVIDIA invested billions of dollars to support ASE subsidiary Siliconware Precision Industries (SPIL) in expanding CoWoS capacity (including new cleanrooms and equipment), making advanced packaging an AI bottleneck; Yole forecasts advanced packaging capex to approach $28 billion in 2026, surpassing traditional packaging for the first time — intensified crowding out as packaging/testing and substrate resources are shared with HVAC board cards
